timeAndOwnership.clockFloorTrust: clockFloorMs is an independent caller-trusted input; it is not derived from the bundle and is not a trusted cross-restart clock service.
timeAndOwnership.clockRollbackCoverage: Only nowMs below the supplied floor is detected as rollback, in addition to not-yet-valid and expired bundle checks. Rollback that remains above the supplied floor is not proven detectable.
timeAndOwnership.replay: Same-request replay inside the original expiry preserves collectedAt, expiresAt, bytes and mtime; it does not renew evidence. Expired or conflicting requests do not overwrite the bundle.
timeAndOwnership.ownerIncarnation: fenceIntentDigest and fenceExclusiveDigest bind the currently observed owner incarnation. Owner death/takeover invalidates the old expected context and old package; a new owner must re-observe and use an explicit new output directory.

nativeAndConcurrencyCoverage: A parent holds the real fence while a delegated child validates the parent owner context, writes the bundle and really exits with code 86 before completion. A new child under the same living owner and expected context observes verify rejecting the incomplete output, completes the record without rewriting the bundle, and cold verification succeeds.

After an owner child dies, a new owner takes over the fence. Old expected context and old output fail, old bytes remain untouched, and only a newly observed context with an explicit new directory succeeds.

Four in-process same-directory create requests leave exactly one bundle and one completion record; rejected requests are explicit conflicts and a differing TTL cannot overwrite the persisted bytes. This is not a claim of multi-process concurrency coverage.
